Sargent & Lundy (2023). Capital Cost and Performance Characteristic Estimates for Utility Scale Electric Power Generating Technologies, Report SL-018001, Final - Rev A, 6 December 2023, prepared for the U.S. Energy Information Administration and Z Federal; published by U.S. EIA, January 2024, as Capital Cost and Performance Characteristics for Utility-Scale Electric Power Generating Technologies (AEO2025 assumptions). Washington, DC: U.S. Department of Energy, EIA.

Printed page numbers (PDF page = printed page + 42; roman-numbered front matter cited as p.III). Loaded the heat-relevant cases 1-11: USC coal with and without 95% capture, aeroderivative and H-class simple-cycle CTs, H-class combined cycles (2x2x1, 1x1x1 single shaft, and the 95%-capture case), woody-biomass BFB with 95% capture, AP1000 and 6x80 MW SMR nuclear, 50 MW binary geothermal. Skipped cases 12-19 (hydro, onshore/offshore wind, PV, PV+storage, battery). The report has no CSP, no fuel cell, no CHP and no electric boiler case, and the 2023 report gives no 2030/2050 projections (one 2023 reference case each, so no separate year processes). Per case: net capacity, overnight capital cost $/kW net (EPC plus owner costs, excl. financing), fixed O&M, variable O&M, electric efficiency from net heat rate (HHV where printed; nuclear basis not stated), operating life (40 y), construction time, CO2 rate from Table 1-2, share-to-capture for capture cases. Money is 2023 USD as stated in every table. Traps: (1) all per kW or MWh of ELECTRIC output, no heat output; (2) cases 2, 7, 8 are whole plants with capture (INCLUDES CAPTURE); case 7 gives capture equipment and labor separately (other-values only); (3) geothermal case excludes well drilling and field costs (wells assumed drilled; EGS not costed); (4) CT case 4 variable O&M excludes the per-start major maintenance cost (23,100 USD/start, other-values); (5) the summary table (p.III) rounds capex (e.g. 836 vs printed 835.5 in the case table; case table used); (6) CC case 7 capture cases consume steam from the HRSG, hence the lower net output (543 vs 627 MW).
